The 29 first-round HACS variants, RuHACS and a recently reported HACS from Actinomycetospora chiangmaiensis (AcHACS), as well as known oxalyl-CoA decarboxylases (OXCs), including EcOXC, OfOXC, Methylobacterium extorquens OXC (MeOXC) and its engineered variant MeOXC4 were screened in the 96 well plate-based resting cell bioconversion system described in the previous section (Figure 26A-C). A phylogenetic analysis of the first-round variants showed that the distances of variants are well spread out throughout the phylogenetic tree, from very close homologs of RuHACS, such as HACS-1-2 to distant homologs, such as HACS-1-8, and HACS-1-11 on either end of the tree (Figure 26D). Based on the screening results, three (HACS-1- 15, 19, and 20) out of 29 first-round variants showed glycolate production, with HACS-1- 15 (HACS from Alphaproteobacteria bacterium, ApbHACS, previously referred to as BsmHACS) and HACS-1-20 (HACS from Dehalococcoidia bacterium, DhcHACS) showing substantially higher glycolate flux compared to RuHACS and MeOXC4 (Figure 26D). It is worth noting that both ApbHACS and DhcHACS belong to the same subclade as RuHACS (highlighted in green in Figure 26D). Interestingly, AcHACS, which is phylogenetically distant from all first-round variants and was reported to catalyze reversible cleavage of 2-hydroxyisobutyryl-CoA to acetone and formyl-CoA, also showed activity for C1-C1 condensation at similar level as RuHACS (Figure 26D). To assess their performance at physiologically relevant conditions, we investigated the 36 active variants at low formaldehyde concentration (0.5 mM). Under this condition, ApbHACS and DhcHACS exhibited an even larger increase in glycolate flux when compared to RuHACS (7-fold and 6-fold, respectively), suggesting improved affinity of these variants towards formaldehyde. Kinetic parameters of the purified enzymes further corroborate this result and revealed that ApbHACS (K = 8.8 mM) has a lower M apparent K toward formaldehyde than DhcHACS (K = 12.1 mM), while DhcHACS (k M M cat = 7.8 s-1) has better turnover frequency than ApbHACS (k = 4.7 s-1) (Table 5). Both cat variants exhibit substantially improved apparent K and turnover toward both M formaldehyde and formyl-CoA compared to RuHACS with more than 5-fold and 6-fold improvement in catalytic efficiency (k /K ) toward formaldehyde and 3-fold and 7.5-fold cat M toward formyl-CoA for ApbHACS and DhcHACS, respectively (Table 5).
